# Baseline Results

Phase 4 (W8-9) exit-criterion baseline metrics for both shipped configs, computed by tools/generate_baseline_results.py from real sim.driver.run_simulation() runs (seed=42, duration_s=172800.0, dt_s=10.0) aggregated by sim.metrics.compute_metrics().

Two delivery figures are reported and they answer different questions. *Delivery success rate* counts every item downlinked before the end of the 48 h run, however late. *Deadline success ratio* counts only items downlinked at or before their own deadline (TT&C 300 s, SSTV 3600 s, CODEC2_M17 900 s after arrival; sim/data_arrival.py), divided by all generated items. Under sparse single-station passes most items are delivered late, so the two differ by an order of magnitude.

Energy per delivered bit uses the explicit comms-state -> transmit-class power mapping of docs/decisions/0009-explicit-transmit-class-power-mapping.md: Config B/C's collapsed COMMS_ACTIVE state is charged the transmit draw of the data class it is serving (before decision 0009 it fell through to the idle draw).

Config A and Config B's numbers below may now differ beyond energy per delivered bit: this driver fires real `PASS_END`/`POWER_LOW`/recovery events (Phase 5, Task 2), so Config A's autonomous safe-mode recovery and Config B's ground-only recovery (SIM-011) can now produce genuinely different outcomes.

Config C (Phase 7D) is a synthetic third configuration — not a POQUITO/SomaiyaSat mission variant like Config A/B — added to test the engine's generality claim against a deployment x recovery-model axis combination neither shipped config represents (single-path deployment + autonomous-permitted recovery). Its row below is generated against the DUAL ground-station reference scenario (sim.scenario.GROUND_STATIONS_DUAL, Phase 7B), not the single-station default Config A/B use — so Config C's numbers are not directly comparable to A/B's on ground-station coverage; see docs/decisions/0006-config-c-generality-axis.md for the full scope statement, including what Config C deliberately does NOT extend (policy comparison, the RQ1-RQ3 visualization dashboard).

## Config config-a

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Delivery success rate (delivered within run window / generated) | 91.85% |
| Deadline success ratio (delivered by deadline / generated) | 2.61% |
| TT&C latency min (s) | 3.758 |
| TT&C latency median (s) | 19911.441 |
| TT&C latency p95 (s) | 39819.859 |
| TT&C latency max (s) | 42723.430 |
| Energy per delivered bit (J/bit) | 0.000338873 |

### Per-class delivery breakdown

The aggregate delivery success rate and deadline-miss counts above average over all classes; this table breaks the same run down by data class so that a class the frozen priority scheduler starves entirely (delivered = 0) is visible rather than folded into the aggregate. "Delivered (late)" and "Never delivered" are both counted in the deadline-misses table above, but are distinct outcomes: the former means the item eventually arrived at the ground, just after its deadline; the latter means it was still queued, undelivered, at the end of the run.

| Data class | Arrived | Delivered (on time) | Delivered (late) | Never delivered | Deadline success ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TTC | 915 | 10 | 836 | 69 | 1.09% |
| SSTV | 202 | 17 | 164 | 21 | 8.42% |
| CODEC2_M17 | 184 | 7 | 161 | 16 | 3.80% |

### Deadline misses by class

| Data class | Deadline misses |
|---|---|
| TTC | 904 |
| SSTV | 178 |
| CODEC2_M17 | 175 |
